summary: Cross-account assume-role failures due to role-tag assertion policy mismatch after provisioner change
description: Issue summary: Several internal services (provisioner, account-broker) started receiving AccessDenied when calling sts:AssumeRole for cross-account operations. This began immediately after a change to the provisioner that started asserting a role attribute tag 'redwood-env' on newly created roles. Impact: cross-account debug runs, Dedicated provisioning jobs, and scheduled maintenance workflows are failing intermittently; some customer onboards delayed. Environment: production, us-east-1. Observed behavior: sts:AssumeRole calls return AccessDenied with Condition mismatch in CloudTrail logs; role exists and trust relationship is valid. Expectation: assume-role should succeed when principal session tags match policy conditions or when tag assertion is not required.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create a new role in account B with provisioner v2.3.1 which sets tag 'redwood-env=prod'.
2) From account A, call sts:AssumeRole with session tags 'redwoodEnv=prod' (legacy agent).
3) Observe AccessDenied in the response and 'Condition Key mismatch' entries in CloudTrail for sts:AssumeRole.
logs_excerpt:
CloudTrail event (sts:AssumeRole) shows: errorCode=AccessDenied, errorMessage=Not authorized to perform sts:AssumeRole, condition: StringEquals:aws:PrincipalTag/redwood-env != 'prod'
Relevant IAM role tag list: [ {Key: 'RedwoodEnv', Value: 'prod'}, {Key: 'owner', Value: 'infra-team'} ]
investigation_notes: Initial findings: After comparing the provisioner change (PR #2156) we confirmed it started writing 'redwood-env' as a tag on roles. Org policy enforcement layer normalizes tags to PascalCase ('RedwoodEnv') and strips dashes for legacy compatibility. AssumeRole calls from older agents still send session tags using camelCase 'redwoodEnv'. The trust policy uses Condition: StringEquals: aws:PrincipalTag/redwood-env = 'prod' which does not match the normalized tag key. CloudTrail and STS deny message corroborate a tag-key mismatch rather than missing trust. GCP service accounts observed no change; impact is limited to AWS cross-account role flows. Hypothesis: tag key normalization during role creation caused discrepancy between tag keys referenced in the Condition and actual principal tags presented during AssumeRole, causing denies.
mitigation_performed: Temporary mitigation applied 2026-03-11: updated the provisioner to set both normalized and legacy tag keys when creating roles (RedwoodEnv and redwood-env). Rolled this change to prod in us-east-1 provisioner fleet. Added a short-lived fallback in the account-broker to rewrite session tags to include both camelCase and dashed keys. This restored most failing workflows within 90 minutes.
next_steps:
1) Engineering: update org-policy normalization doc and provisioner so tags are written in three canonical forms (redwood-env, redwoodEnv, RedwoodEnv) where allowed. (owner: infra-provisioning)
2) Security: review trust policies that reference tag keys and migrate them to use aws:RequestTag/TaggedCondition where possible, or use TagKey alias mapping. (owner: secops)
3) SRE: schedule a canary rollout of the provisioner 2.3.2 with the canonical tag strategy and monitor STS deny rate for 48h. (owner: oncall)
4) Postmortem: prepare incident write-up and update runbook with tag-key compatibility guidance. (owner: postmortem-team)

2026-03-10 10:05 - Ethan Cole: Confirmed CloudTrail denies point to Condition mismatch on principal tag key. Adding infra-provisioning to investigate tag writes.

2026-03-10 13:41 - Maya Liu (infra-provisioning): Found PR 2156 changed tag key to 'redwood-env' to be explicit. Org-wide tag normalizer converts '-' to PascalCase which is causing divergence. Reverting will be disruptive; proposing dual-write.

2026-03-11 01:17 - Ethan Cole: Deployed hotfix to provisioner that writes both legacy and normalized tag keys. Account-broker also updated to map session tags. Monitoring deny rate; preliminary metrics look good.

2026-03-12 08:30 - Priya Nambiar: Requesting security review before we permanently change trust policies. Also need to schedule a 48h canary for the dual-write approach and then reconcile tags across existing roles using a backfill job.
2026-03-12 11:05 - Security (Ana Perez): Acknowledged. We'll perform a risk assessment and provide recommended policy migration steps by EOD 2026-03-13.
resolution: In progress: temporary dual-write mitigation applied; most workflows restored. Permanent fix requires coordinated policy migration and a provisioner update to write canonical tag forms. Security review scheduled. Full resolution target: backfill existing role tags and update trust policies to reference canonical keys or support aliases.
workaround: Provisioner dual-writes both 'redwood-env' and 'RedwoodEnv' tags; account-broker rewrites session tags before AssumeRole. Use direct cross-account assume with explicit sts:TagSession calls for critical job reruns while fix is rolling out.
estimated_risk: Medium - potential for missed denies in other regions if rollout is inconsistent; requires careful rollforward with monitoring
owner_notes: Do not revert PR 2156 without a migration plan. Any backfill script must be idempotent and rate-limited to avoid API throttling in customer accounts.
